Prevention: Allow adequate spacing (2-3 feet apart) between plants to improve airflow in the canopy.
Plant in raised beds for improved drainage and airflow
Prune regularly to prevent shading of berries by thick foliage that creates ideal conditions for disease development
Use drip irrigation as it provides a direct source of water and eliminates excess moisture on fruit and leaves.
Monitoring: Look out for spreading brown rot and fuzzy gray mold on ripening berries.
Check for light brown to black slightly sunken, circular or irregular surface lesions on the fruit that are covered with gray dusty powder.
Check out for infected berries that remain firm but are covered with gray molds and mycelium
Look for fruit that are completely rotten dry, tough and mummified.
Take action when 3% of the crop is affected.
Direct Control: Select a site with good soil drainage and air circulation to minimize development of the disease
Pick fruit frequently and early in the day as soon as plants are dry.
Keep the berries in a cool place immediately after harvest.
Trichoderma harzinium at 1.5g/2.5L water every 10 -12 weeks
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
